raw_text:
Recently, warnings from researchers inside the world’s largest artificial intelligence labs about the rapid pace of development have led to panic about the possibility that the technology could extinguish humanity. Those warnings are predicated on the idea that—propelled by ferocious competition and a rivalry between the US and China—labs are barreling toward superintelligent models whose abilities will far surpass those of humans.
But according to Father Paolo Benanti, a priest who advises the Catholic Church on AI, the handwaving over superintelligence distracts from the need for open debate about how to constrain the companies building the technology. By casting the problem as so complex that only they can solve it, he says, the big labs exclude everyone else from the conversation.
“Ethics cannot be something that belongs to the board of trustees of a company. It’s something that has to be balanced, mitigated in debate in the public square.” Benanti tells WIRED. “We need democratic regulation.”
In an essay published on the heels of the safety warnings, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for new AI models to undergo mandatory third-party evaluations prior to release, and some sort of crackdown on distillation, a process where rival labs train their own AI on the outputs of proprietary models. Others have argued for a total ban on recursive self-improvement, where AI uses its advanced coding capabilities to help develop future iterations of itself.
Benanti is less interested in restricting methods for developing AI, which he fears could quash innovation, and more so in establishing standards that ensure models cannot slip from human control. Whatever shape those standards take, he says, they should not be designed by the labs.
“The narrative of the frontier labs is self-interested, to gain or maintain a position in the market,” says Benanti. When a small group of companies dictates the rules under which an industry operates, he says, “this has a really clear name: a cartel.”
It’s difficult to know how seriously to take grand pronouncements about the capabilities of the latest and future AI models, says Benanti, owing to the overlapping economic, political, and personal incentives at play.
While both OpenAI and Anthropic have supported calls for a slowdown in development, they’re also preparing to go public, and there are many billions of dollars at stake for whoever captures the market. The animosity between the US and China, where the most advanced AI models are being developed, also complicates the picture.
Anthropic declined to comment. OpenAI and Google DeepMind did not respond to requests for comment.
Benanti also takes issue with the way certain corners of the AI industry talk about superintelligence, with the kind of reverence typically reserved for a god: as sophisticated beyond our understanding, practically omnipotent. (OpenAI CEO Sam Altman once said he aspires to build a “magic intelligence in the sky.”) That kind of framing, Benanti says, threatens to skew the discourse about the technology.
“Are we talking about some-thing, or some-one? This is the real difference. It’s not a matter of faith, it’s a matter of mathematics,” he says. “We are not building the next divinity. We are simply deluding ourselves that there is something more than statistical computation [going on].”
By raising questions about what separates man and machine, and how to shield future generations from the negative effects of technology, the advent of AI has the potential to create “a new role for religions in public debate,” says Benanti. “Living the challenge of the time is part of the mission of the Church.”
Though Benanti is a member of the priesthood, he does not formally represent the Holy See, the governing body of the Catholic Church. Instead, he counsels the church in his capacity as a scholar of philosophy, theology, and technology. Benanti tells WIRED he uses AI to help create tools and materials for his university students, but declined to specify how Pope Leo XIV engages with the technology, if at all. (Benanti’s staff say he is bound by an “oath of secrecy.”)
In May, Pope Leo published his first-ever encyclical, a letter that applies religious teachings to the problems of the day and clarifies the position of the Church. He chose artificial intelligence as its subject.
In the letter, the Pope warned against the technocratic logic that runs through the AI industry, which presents “efficiency as the ultimate measure of value,” and casts human beings as “a project to be optimized.” He also called for international collaboration between rival superpowers and AI companies, who he said must set aside the “desire to secure geopolitical or commercial dominance” to ensure that the technology is developed in service of the common good. In one particularly prescient section, he warned of “the danger of humanity becoming a victim of its own achievements.”
The flap over superintelligence and existential risk threatens to distract from the ambitions laid out in the encyclical, says Benanti, by encouraging people to forfeit their say in the direction the technology should take to a small group of mathematicians, computer scientists, and executives at the big labs.
“The first thing is, we need to have brakes, and a wheel,” says Benanti. “That means a significant position of control for human beings over the machine.”

HC frees Ghaziabad woman from father's custody to join Muslim husband
Chauhan said she was 26 years old, had completed her BA and had married Akbar Khan.
The Allahabad high court on Tuesday allowed a 26-year-old Ghaziabad woman to leave her father’s custody and live with her Muslim husband, holding that an adult is entitled to choose her life partner and live according to her own wishes.
Justice Sandeep Jain passed the order on a habeas corpus petition, filed in September 2025, in connection with Sonika Chauhan, who was produced before the court on Tuesday in compliance with its September 8 order. She was brought to the court by a sub-inspector and a woman constable from Indirapuram police station.
During her interaction with the court, Chauhan said she was 26 years old, had completed her BA and had married Akbar Khan. She said she wanted to live with him and alleged that her father had confined her at home because he disapproved of her marriage.
Khan also appeared before the court and expressed his willingness to live with Chauhan.
Her father, Lakshman Singh Chauhan, however, alleged that his daughter had been blackmailed by Khan and was acting under his pressure.
After interacting with all the parties, the court held that a person who has attained age of majority has the fundamental right to choose a life partner and live according to her own wishes.
Such a choice, it said, is personal to the individual and cannot be dictated or controlled by the wishes of parents or other family members.
The court accordingly held that Chauhan was at liberty to live with Khan and directed the police to provide adequate security to the couple. It also directed the family members not to interfere in their matrimonial life.

2 UP cops, 2 CRPF personnel held for 'gangrape' of woman in Amroha
Amroha , Two Uttar Pradesh Police personnel and two CRPF personnel have been arrested for the alleged gangrape of a woman from Haryana at a farmhouse in Amroha district, an official said on Wednesday.
The alleged incident took place in the Hasanpur area of Amroha. A sub-inspector and a head constable posted at the Hasanpur police station and a sub-inspector and a head constable of the Central Reserve Police Force have been arrested in connection with the incident.
According to Superintendent of Police Lakhan Singh Yadav, the woman, aged about 24 years and a resident of Haryana's Fatehabad, has alleged that she was contacted on September 20 by a female acquaintance, who asked her to meet CRPF Inspector Mohit, a resident of Saurang village in Muzaffarnagar district, to visit religious places in Amroha.
The rape survivor allegedly met Mohit at Haryana's Sonipat on September 21. From there, they travelled to Meerut, where Mohit was joined by his colleague, CRPF Head Constable Lalaram Yadav, a resident of Rajasthan's Alwar.
On the evening of September 22, the two men allegedly took the woman to Hasanpur in a car and picked up Sub-Inspector Sanjay Tomar on their way.
The trio then took her to a farmhouse on the Atrasi-Hasanpur road, where they rented two rooms.
According to the complaint, police Head Constable Pramod had arranged food and liquor for the group.
Later in the evening, Mohit, Yadav and Tomar allegedly took turns to rape the woman. Pramod then entered the room and attempted to rape her, but she managed to push him out, locked the door, and searched online for the police helpline number.
The rape survivor contacted police at around 6 am on Wednesday.
Teams from the Hasanpur and Rajabpur police stations rushed to the spot, took the woman to safety and apprehended all four accused.
"Based on the victim's complaint, an FIR has been registered against the four accused under the relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for abduction or enticement and gangrape. All four have been arrested and remanded in judicial custody," the SP said.
Departmental proceedings have been initiated against the local sub-inspector following his suspension and a report has been sent to senior CRPF authorities, recommending strict disciplinary action against the two paramilitary personnel, he added.
According to Hasanpur Kotwali in-charge Amar Pal Singh, the farmhouse where the alleged incident took place reportedly belongs to an independent MLA from Uttarakhand.
Police have questioned the manager of the property and further investigation is underway.
Reacting to the incident, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav said in a social-media post that when governance is based on crime, the police force also becomes corrupt.
Referring to the alleged gangrape of the woman in Amroha, the former Uttar Pradesh chief minister said the incident is a "stain" on the police force that no amount of patronage can erase.
He demanded "historic action" in the matter.

Everything announced at Meta Connect 2026
VR glasses, Aviator-style Ray-Ban Meta specs, Ace Attorney in virtual reality and much more.
It's Meta's turn to reveal new hardware during the always-busy fall season. The company showed off two new types of wearables at Meta Connect, virtual reality glasses and an audio-only set, as well as the third-gen Ray-Ban Meta AI specs.
It announced some updates for Meta Ray-Ban Display while making those smart glasses more broadly available. In addition, Meta revealed a hearing assistance feature for its glasses along with the biggest changes yet for Beat Saber and a raft of entertainment content that's coming to the VR ecosystem. In addition, Meta is working on bringing the Muse AI agent to its glasses.
Let's dive into everything the company announced at Meta Connect 2026. You can also check out our liveblog for a real-time breakdown of all the announcements.
Meta VR Glasses
The biggest announcement at Meta Connect was the company's virtual reality glasses. Rumors back in 2023 suggested that Meta would deploy its first such product in 2027 and it's sticking to that time frame — Meta VR Glasses will arrive next spring. You might want to start putting some cash aside for them if you're interested, though, as they'll cost $1,300.
The company says, at around 100 grams, Meta VR Glasses are five times lighter than the Meta Quest 3 headset. The frames are built with magnesium alloy and have pancake lenses. They include full-color passthrough video support and a 5K display. Meta claims they'll offer "cinema-grade clarity" with support for Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos spatial audio. The company says it's the first IMAX Enhanced certified VR device too.
All of the computing is handled by a tethered puck and everything runs on Qualcomm's Snapdragon Reality Elite chipset. The puck also contains the storage and battery. Meta says the glasses will be able to deliver "up to three hours of continuous high-resolution media playback" on a charge. The puck has support for 45W fast charging too.
At the outset, there'll be 75 games you can play using hand gestures. The glasses will run every game that's available for Quest headsets with the help of support for Touch Plus controllers. You'll be able to stream titles through Xbox Cloud Gaming, though Microsoft is imposing new time limits on that service. There's the option to connect to other gaming devices wirelessly or via USB-C as well.
True to its metaverse-derived name, Meta sees the glasses as a vector for productivity. You can hook the device up to a Windows PC or Mac and control them with a virtual keyboard and touchpad on a desk or table. You can just use a physical mouse and keyboard too.
Not unlike Apple Vision Pro, Meta VR Glasses will support holographic avatars that you can use in video calls on apps such as WhatsApp and Zoom. Folks who are joining a call on a flatscreen device can see your hologram. When you see another person's hologram while you're using the VR Glasses, spatial audio will place their voice in their virtual location.
Of course, the company is integrating Meta AI into the glasses. You can tell Meta VR Glasses what you want to do using your voice. Alternatively, you can control the device with your eyes or hand gestures.
Ray-Ban Meta Audio
Perhaps in an effort to sidestep the not-unwarranted "pervert glasses" label that many have given to wearables that have a camera, Meta is releasing an audio-only model. The Ray-Ban Meta Audio glasses are, of course, equipped with an AI voice assistant. They support music and podcast playback as well as voice calls. The company says the device will run for up to 12 hours on a charge. The charging case is said to add up to 48 hours of use.
Ray-Ban Meta Audio is designed for all-day wear, the company notes. The glasses weigh 43 grams and have "professionally adjustable temple tips, adjustable or swappable nose pads and overextension hinges." They'll be available in a classic Ray-Ban style called Clubmaster and a more rectangular Burbank shape in 23 color and lens combos. The glasses support prescription lenses too.
Pre-orders for the Ray-Ban Meta Audio open today and the glasses ship on October 13. They start at $349.
Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 and other smart glasses
Meta still does have camera-equipped smart glasses, however. It has refreshed the Ray-Ban Meta with a slimmer design and a button that triggers Meta AI. The third-gen model is said to have a longer battery life than the previous one, with nine hours of usage versus eight. There's a six-mic array that Meta claims can cut out over 90 percent of background noise for clearer audio.
The 12MP camera supports 3K video capture. The company adds that the cameras on its AI glasses will soon be able to record videos with Dolby Atmos spatial audio. A dynamic photo feature can snap multiple shots and you can pick the best one (or let Meta AI suggest options).
You can now get the glasses in the style of Ray-Ban's classic Aviator, as well as Zena, a cat-eye frame. The Wayfarer look is sticking around too. Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 are available starting today in 27 combos of lenses and colors. They start at $449.
There are a bunch of special editions as well. An Aviator version in milky beige with brown Transitions lenses start at $579 and will be available for a limited time. There are new collabs with Kylie Jenner and Blackpink's Lisa, and those models start at $399. Meta is also releasing new styles for its Essilor Luxottica glasses and bringing them (and other models) to more markets.
On top of all of that, Meta is introducing more models in its own-brand Meta Glasses range. The Meta Adventurer frames now start at $249 with a black frame and gray lenses along with a plug-in case, and there's also a limited-edition version of the Meta Fury with a clear frame and mirrored lenses. Pre-orders for the former open today and they'll hit shelves on October 23.
Meta Ray-Ban Display updates
There were updates on the Meta Ray-Ban Display front as well. Meta is bringing this model to more markets and making them more broadly available in the US, where you can now order them online for $799. Folks in the UK and Canada can buy these glasses today for £749 and $1,149 CAD, respectively. Pre-orders are opening today in Germany, France and Italy, where Meta Ray-Ban Display starts at €899. The glasses will be available in those three countries on October 13.
In terms of feature updates, folks in the US and Canada will be able to access cycling and public transit directions in the heads-up navigation tool later this month. Also, instead of turn-by-turn walking directions, the glasses can tell you to turn at a certain landmark that's in front of you.
Meta Ray-Ban Display will support holograms in video calls too, but you'll need to capture yourself using the Meta AI app if you want to create your own avatar. This will first be supported for WhatsApp calls in the US this fall.
Through the Meta AI app and Explore (an app you can access on the glasses), you'll be able to check out an array of web apps. Moreover, Meta Ray-Ban Display will support photo editing on the display, Dolby Atmos video capture, notifications mirrored from your phone and more.
Hearing enhancement feature
Meta is bringing a hearing enhancement feature to its smart glasses. It's designed more for people who can usually hear fine but might struggle in a noisy environment than hard-of-hearing folks who would benefit more from an actual hearing aid.
The setup flow is similar to the hearing aid feature on Apple's AirPods — you'll need to listen to tones in a quiet room so the glasses can tune the settings for you. You can switch this mode on or off by saying "Hey Meta, start hearing enhancement."
This feature will be available in the US later this year on Meta Glasses, and later on the third-gen Ray-Ban Meta and Ray-Ban Meta Audio. There's a 30-day trial but the company says it'll cost a one-off $149 fee after that. Alternatively, it's included with a Meta One subscription. Meta says the hearing enhancement tool is eligible for FSA and HSA reimbursement.
Beat Saber, Supernatural's return and other VR games
Let's get into the entertainment side of VR, starting with Beat Saber. Meta-owned developer Beat Games is said to be giving the title its biggest update ever this spring. It includes support for hand tracking, so you'll no longer need to use Touch Plus controllers to play, though you can still do that if you prefer.
Flux is a new single-player mode in which you can use powers like the Flux Tether. Meta says this "channels power between your palms to slice through notes in time with the beat of pulse-pounding tracks." Flux, which will be available on Meta VR Glasses and Meta Quest, includes 35 songs from across the Beat Saber landscape at the outset, with more to follow.
Beat Games is also revamping the single-player campaign to include a narrative aspect, fresh missions and a new menu system. The studio is adding a new progression and rewards system as well. This will let you customize the look and sound of the game.
Supernatural will be back on the Meta Horizon Store this fall. A newly independent development team took the reins of the VR exercise platform after Meta made widescale cuts across its VR and metaverse division at the start of the year. Users' points, streaks and badges will remain intact in the new app. The developers are adding more HD environments, workouts and music along with other upgrades, Meta says.
Elsewhere on the gaming front, heist title Payday: Aces High is coming to Meta Quest 3 and 3S later this year with support for co-op crossplay with the PC VR version. An open playtest starts October 19. A mixed reality version of Tetris Effect is coming to Meta VR Glasses next year with hand-tracking support. Two Point Hospital is on the way to Meta Quest 3 and 3S with hand-tracking support as well.
While fans wait for the first entirely new Ace Attorney game in over a decade, the series is about to make its VR debut. Phoenix Wright Ace Attorney: Dual Destinies (which was first released on the Nintendo DS in 2013) is coming to Meta VR Glasses and Meta Quest next year with support for hand tracking and voice activation, so you can physically point at witnesses and yell "objection!" I've gotta say, that sounds like a fun way to confuse people you live with. You can check out Phoenix Wright Ace Attorney: Dual Destinies VR on Meta VR Glasses and Meta Quest next year.
VR movies, sports and other entertainment
Meta is making a bigger push into 3D and VR experiences on its headsets and Meta VR Glasses. Disney+ subscribers (that service just got more expensive in the US, FYI) in certain countries will be able to stream the likes of The Avengers and Black Panther in 3D starting in November.
Meta VR Glasses owners will be able to check out VR Enhanced versions of iconic films like Avengers: Infinity War and Star Wars: A New Hope next spring. Meta says, in the versions of these movies that will be available through a new Disney Immersive Cinema by ILM app, "your surroundings will be transformed with immersive environments, dynamic effects, stunning 3D visuals and spatial audio to feel like you're not just watching a scene, but living inside it."
A docuseries called Open Season will debut in the Meta Quest TV app on September 29. This will take you inside the therapy sessions of Golden State Warriors player and four-time NBA champion Draymond Green during the 2025-26 season. This is the first entry in an original series called Meta Presents.
The company says it will offer hundreds of 2D and 3D movies for folks to buy and rent in the US later this year. It will expand the library to more countries by the time Meta VR Glasses are available.
A new National Geographic: Beyond app will feature 180-degree 3D experiences of the natural world. A whole bunch of other streaming apps are available too, including Amazon Prime Video, YouTube, DirecTV, AMC+, Crunchyroll, Plex and Tubi, while Peacock, HBO Max and Paramount+ will offer up 3D titles.
Meta says that, along with being able to dive into sports apps like those from the NBA and MLB, you can check out immersive sports from ESPN. This will include 8K streaming with 180-degree views. Immersive Sports starts with college football this year, and it'll expand to other sports in 2027. On Meta VR Glasses, you'll be able to watch more than 100 live sports events each year via Meta's partnerships with MLB, NBC Sports, TNT Sports and UFC.
One more thing
We know barely anything about it, but at the end of today's keynote, Zuckerberg briefly showed off a new device called Muse Charm. It's a dedicated piece of hardware that houses your personal Muse Agent with a small display, speakers, mics and a fingerprint sensor. It looks a little like a Tamagotchi, into which, Zuckerberg says, Meta has "packed the whole Muse experience, including the real-time voice and avatar stack into something that fits on a keychain and is always available to talk to." The company says it'll have more to share on the device later this year.

WASHINGTON – In her opening statement for tomorrow’s hearing before a key Senate committee, Trump’s pick to lead the Food and Drug Administration, Heidi Overton, plans to emphasize the need for speed and efficiency at the FDA to compete with China’s accelerating biotechnology industry.
“President Trump’s direction for me in this role, should I be confirmed, is to ‘go fast.’” Overton says in the statement, an advance copy of which was obtained by STAT. “Slow and prohibitive requirements for cutting edge therapies at the FDA means investment is increasingly flowing to China who has found ways to do things faster and cheaper.”
Overton says she is committed to continuing the work the administration began earlier this year to speed up the clinical trial process through Operation Trailblazer, and says that she will “work with the dedicated career professionals to make sure every aspect of clinical trials and drug development is optimized to get cures to patients faster and that every person at FDA shares those goals.”

Bentley has taken the covers off its first-ever fully electric car, the Torcal, making it the automaker's fourth model line, joining the Continental GT, the Flying Spur sedan, and the Bentayga SUV. The luxury brand is confident about the launch, too, with Bentley chairman and CEO Frank-Steffen Walliser saying he believes “this is one of the best Bentleys ever.”
When WIRED first reported on the car in July, we said the EV would have more than 300 miles of range. Well, turns out it has considerably more: up to 375 miles (on the WLTP cycle, maybe 330 miles on EPA), and can charge from 10 to 80 percent in just 16 minutes at 400 kilowatts.
Prodigious performance from a motor on each axle sees the five-seat Torcal—smaller than the Bentayga and so perhaps more of an urban SUV—get 888 metric horsepower (PS) and 1,350 Newton-meters (Nm) of torque in the sporting S models, resulting in 0 to 60 mph in as little as 2.9 seconds and a top speed of 162 mph. The “core" model drops to 821 PS and 1,194 Nm, with standstill to 60 mph in 3.4 seconds, and a max of 155 mph.
However, luxury brands get worried about their existing client bases when they switch to electric vehicles—look to Ferrari as a prime example—so it's no surprise that Bentley is keen to point out how this new model embodies the finest elements of the brand, just like every other high-end marque does going into electrification. “The Torcal is a Bentley first and foremost," says the launch literature. “In every aspect of its design, technology, craftsmanship, materials, and sustainability, it is a template for future Bentleys, regardless of powertrain.”
The reason for leaning into brand heritage is obvious on dealership lots. The first-ever EV Bentley will roll off the production line into a decidedly twitchy luxury auto market where Lamborghini shelved its Lanzador electric GT—with CEO Stephan Winkelmann stating demand among its buyers was “going almost to zero, if not to zero”—and Mercedes-Benz selling just 1,450 of its electric G Wagen in Europe through April 2025. Rolls-Royce Spectre sales are down nearly by half, with the brand hoping that a model refresh will turn things around.
And make no mistake that the Torcal is aiming for the luxury dollar. At $218,000 or £173,300 for the base model, and $258,200 or £199,300 for the First Edition S, this EV is priced higher than the Range Rover Electric, which has a similar range and starts in the US at $138,000. But a fairer comparison to the Torcal would be the Range Rover Electric Autobiography model, which clocks in at $208,000. Keep that in mind, and it's easy to see that Bentley is trying to take market share from JLR with its new SUV: spend an extra $10,000, people, and you can drive off in an electric Bentley instead of a Range Rover.
At 4,983 mm long (161 mm shorter than a Bentayga) and 2,016 mm in width, the Torcal is not far off the size of the Range Rover Electric, but the most drastic difference is in height. The Range Rover Electric towers over the Torcal by nearly 20 centimeters. Also, while Bentley insists the Torcal has off-road chops, it's probably safe to say the Range Rover Electric will have it pipped there.
Where Bentley wants the Torcal to pull ahead is in the luxury refinements. Despite being smaller than its stablemate, the Torcal is a powerful, purposeful-looking SUV, with a switchable glass sunroof and newly designed light clusters, which are particularly evident at the rear. Unlike the Bentayga, the Torcal roofline drops down at the back for better aero efficiency.
At the front, undoubtedly the most striking visual element of the car is the new Torcal grille: Ventilation to a traditional radiator no longer needed, the upright front is now a solid wall of illuminated acrylic “crystals” that light up as you approach, and on a night in a rearview mirror on a freeway or mountain road will be deliberately unsubtle, and a far cry from quiet luxury.
Inside, Bentley continues to ram home the high-end message. All-round power doors open up to reveal a mixture of OLED screens and physical switchgear. The central display curves pleasingly downward, reminiscent of the new Cayenne, but there is deliberately no separate passenger screen option.
Bentley brought in Fox Brothers to engineer a wool tough enough to be used to panel some of the interior, which is apparently a world first. An attractive new wood finish developed for the Torcal is formed from 1,000 layers of walnut off-cuts and recycled paper pressed together, then sliced to less than a millimeter thick. The Torcal has new massage and power-folding seats, and an optional Naim 1,780-watt sound system with 28 speakers including seat shakers and headrest speakers, as well as Dolby Atmos 7.1.
What's impressive is the digital trickery Bentley has employed in both audio and visual manners—mirroring the crystal switchgear, Bentley has created animations on the screens that show light passing through cut glass. After trying to do this completely with computer animation, it was decided the effect was not real enough as the model could not account for minute imperfections in the glass which subtly effect the light patterns cast. So Bentley had to film these animations using real crystal instead. The effect of the central console and instrument panel is striking.
Then to address the sticky issue of driving sound for a pure EV, instead of creating a digital replica of combustion, Bentley decided to shun electronic imitation and recreate the rhythm of a Bentley V8 using real instruments (including drums, viola, and bass guitar) to create a soundscape that, like the glass animations, had subtle variations and tiny imperfections.
Now, this sounds like it might be a terrible idea, but on the very limited demo WIRED heard, it's actually remarkably convincing and will supposedly provide genuine aural feedback to the driver, rather than simply approximately imitating engine notes. Mercifully, for those not looking to keep things rooted in combustion, it can be turned off if you wish. Bentley even went as far as to record indicator sounds (a hammer striking a leather surface) and the digital assistant wake note (the sound of a crystal glass as you run your finger around the rim).
Bentley has thrown in more tech as well: an augmented reality head-up display; a “Refresh” mode that uses light and air for a “more invigorating” cabin environment; facial recognition so the Torcal can set itself up for individual drivers; mobile phone keys; some 25 radars, sensors and cameras for assisted driving systems; and space detection where if another car is encountered on a narrow road, the Torcal can automatically reverse to a point it’s already identified to let the car to pass.
None of this is, in the world of automotive, groundbreaking anymore. Chinese brands are coming for the SUV sector as well, and are offering much more for much less. Take a look at Xiaomi's new SkyNomads. These stacked SUVs are coming to Europe next year and will massively undercut both Bentley and Range Rover. They have more range, more features, and crucially are thinking about car interiors in genuinely new ways, adding built-in projector systems and seating systems that are reconfigurable. The SkyNomad even has a heated floor, for heaven's sake.
Walliser has a simple answer to this threat from Asia, one that is contributing to Bentley's parent Volkswagen Group now cutting 50,000 jobs (though Bentley is doing well financially), and that is to lean into the one thing that Chinese brands cannot copy or improve: heritage. Bentley, founded in 1919, has bags of it. Will it be enough to secure its continued commitment to full-electric cars? Hopefully. I'm not sure that's a winning tactic for the long term.

Americans living in rural areas are increasingly souring on data centers.
In a new poll by the Pew Research Center, which surveyed people in August, half of rural Americans said data centers "are mostly bad for the environment" — a figure substantially higher than in January, when it sat at 32%.
46% of those respondents also said that data centers would drive up home energy costs, up from 32% in January. 45% said they negatively impact the quality of life for those living nearby, while 28% said so in January.
While displeasure with data centers increased among Americans across the board, according to Pew, higher levels of antagonism among rural voters are striking because most data centers are built in rural areas.
The data center buildout, which proponents say is integral for the US to keep pace with China in the AI race, has been suffering a PR crisis as a bipartisan coalition of lawmakers moves to impose limits on data center construction.
Texas Gov. Greg Abbot, who was formerly bullish about building data centers in his state, recently backed away from that optimism. His administration has halted some 1,800 AI data center projects in the state.
All across the country, Americans are rallying to fight against AI data centers, which can cost billions to build and span hundreds of acres. Many are concerned about how the sprawling facilities will affect the environment, utility prices, water resources, and noise levels. Some just don't like AI.
For AI companies like OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, Google, and others, the issue is existential. Without AI data centers, they can't power the products they sell. Sam Altman has recently suggested that new data centers could be built far from where people lived, such as the desert.
Proponents of data centers have said the buildout brings jobs to rural areas. Venture capitalist Gavin Baker recently said that data centers are "probably the best thing that has ever happened to working-class Americans."
Tech bros haven't been able to agree on exactly why Americans aren't taking to the data center buildout. Some have postulated that a Chinese-orchestrated psy-op is behind the distrust, while others said tech leaders haven't sold the product well.
President Donald Trump, for his part, called the data center buildout "the golden goose," and warned against falling behind China.
"The only reason that communities throughout the U.S.A. should not want Data Centers is if they want to end up being backwards and poor," Trump said in August in a Truth Social post.
In the Pew poll, very few Americans — about 4% — said data centers are "good" for the environment, energy costs, and quality of life.
"Americans have grown more negative toward the possible environmental and economic effects of data centers since the beginning of the year," Pew said in a release. "And a majority say they'd be uncomfortable if a new data center started operating in their area."

Imagine walking into a neighbourhood medical store with a prescription in hand. The pharmacist checks the medicine, packs it and hands it over. But what happens when there is no prescription? According to a nationwide survey, for a large number of consumers, the answer is that the medicine may still be sold. The finding comes as the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed installing CCTV cameras at medical stores to make prescription-medicine sales traceable.
The survey, conducted by LocalCircles, saw about 1.06 lakh responses from consumers across 327 districts of India. Of the total respondents, 63% were men and 37% women. Besides, 52% of them were from tier-1 districts, 29% from tier-2 districts and 29% from tier-3, 4 and 5 districts.
The survey found that 64% of consumers said their chemist never or rarely asked for a doctor’s prescription before selling medicines in the past 12 months. Only 15% said their chemist mostly or always refused to sell medicines without a prescription. The survey also found that only 31% of consumers were able to get assistance from a qualified pharmacist most of the time or always, while 13% said they were assisted by someone who was not a qualified pharmacist.
The findings come as the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has floated a draft notification proposing mandatory CCTV surveillance at every medical store that dispenses drugs sold on a doctor’s prescription. Under the proposal, the supply, other than by wholesale, of any drug sold on the prescription of a Registered Medical Practitioner would have to take place under a CCTV surveillance system installed and maintained at the premises.
The proposal also comes against the backdrop of intensified enforcement in multiple States against chemists selling prescription medicines without valid prescriptions, operating without registered pharmacists and failing to provide proper bills.
Neighbourhood chemist remains the main source
The survey found that the neighbourhood chemist remains the primary source of medicines for most consumers. The question on how respondents had primarily purchased medicines in the previous 12 months received 16,822 responses. This revealed that 86% of the respondents primarily depended on local chemists, followed by 14% on ePharmacy apps.
Who is actually behind the counter?
The survey then looked at whether consumers were receiving assistance from qualified pharmacists when they needed help with medicine or disease-related queries. The question received 19,409 responses. 31% of the consumers said they were able to get assistance from a qualified pharmacist most of the time or always. 27% of them said they never or very rarely received such assistance.
Home delivery is not free of the prescription gap
The survey also examined prescription checks when medicines were delivered to consumers’ homes. The question received 15,473 responses. 41% of consumers surveyed said a prescription was never or rarely asked for during home delivery.
A missing bill can mean a missing trail
Consumers were also asked whether they received proper bills when buying medicines from local chemists. Of the 20,573 respondents, 26% said they were not provided a GST bill. “A bill is not merely a tax document. It carries the batch number, expiry date and identity of the seller and provides a record if a medicine turns out to be expired, defective or counterfeit,” it said.
The survey also sought to establish whether consumers had purchased medicines that later turned out to be counterfeit or ineffective. The question received 18,457 responses. 15% of consumers said they had bought medicines that were later found to be fake or counterfeit.

Watch: Six-year-old girl from China sets new Rubik's Cube world record
A young girl has broken the women's world record for the 3x3x3 Rubik's Cube twice in three days at the World Cube Association.
At age six, Lian Yunzhi has become the only female cuber in the world to have an average time under 4.5 seconds. She first broke the record with an average of 4.52 seconds and then 4.27 seconds at competitions in Wuhan and Guangzhou, China.
The young competitor from Sichuan Province has mastered more than 1,300 Rubik's Cube solving algorithms after vigorous training that involved spending two to three hours a day on the cube over the past year.

Ukraine's winter warning to Canada: Help us keep the lights on
Visiting lawmakers urge Ottawa, provinces to help rebuild a battered energy grid
A delegation of Ukrainian parliamentarians called on Canada's federal and provincial governments on Wednesday to help fund electrical transformers as Russia steps up attacks on the Eastern European country's energy grid.
"We are getting ready for the potentially extremely harsh winter," said Ivanna Klympush-Tsintsadze, chair of Ukraine's committee on integration into the European Union.
She said Russia is weaponizing the coming cold weather by focusing attacks on energy infrastructure, water supplies and sewage systems.
"We could have humanitarian disasters of the magnitude that nobody has seen," Klympush-Tsintsadze said.
Throughout the summer Russia has drastically escalated aerial assaults on Ukraine, pounding cities day and night.
Over 800 civilians were killed in July and August, according to the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees.
Moscow has deployed massive, relentless waves of advanced jet-powered drones, ballistic missiles and guided glide bombs to overwhelm air defences.
Klympush-Tsintsadze said Russia's aim is to depopulate the cities and make them unlivable.
She and fellow Ukrainian parliamentarian Oleksandr Merezhko were in Ottawa meeting with Canadian politicians and senior officials and took part in a roundtable discussion with journalists and other Baltic politicians at the Estonian Embassy.
Aside from an urgent, renewed pitch to Canada to sell high-end electronic warfare equipment to combat drones and to help purchase more air-to-air missiles, Klympush-Tsintsadze said they're asking the federal government and provinces to buy into funding packages managed by the Energy Community, an agency of the European Union.
- Ukraine makes some battlefield gains, but 'grey zone' along front is getting bigger
- AnalysisWhat the CIA director’s mystery trip to Moscow says about Putin's next move
Electrical transformers made in North America are not compatible with the ones built in Europe and contributing to the transformer construction ahead of winter would be helpful.
One Canadian province, which Klympush-Tsintsadze declined to name, has already stepped forward and there's a plan to raise the idea with the Ontario government in a meeting on Thursday.
"That's something very specific that can be done," she said.
Merezhko said the war — now four-and-a-half years since the full-scale invasion — is evolving into a more dangerous phase where Ukraine is fighting a "whole coalition" of countries.
"It's not only Russia, which is weak in itself, but it's also Iran, because it provides thousands and thousands of drones. It's also North Korea, which has been providing munitions, continuous, and even armed force, you know, manpower."
His remarks echoed Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who delivered a 26-minute address to the United Nations General Assembly in New York.
Zelenskyy highlighted how Russia is actively globalizing the conflict by drawing in external personnel. He revealed that citizens from 47 countries are being enlisted by Russia to fight. He pleaded with the leaders of those nations to intercede and stop their citizens from being dragged into Moscow's war.
Speaking in English, he also defended Ukraine's strikes on Russia's oil infrastructure.
"Oil itself is not Ukraine's target," Zelenskyy told world leaders. "Our target is Russia's ability to finance this war to drag it out … Russia's finances and Russia's production are what must be stopped if Putin is to be stopped."
He called on the international community to escalate economic sanctions and permanently drain Moscow's war revenues.
In Ottawa, Klympush-Tsintsadze said her view is that the further west she travels from Ukraine, the less the war and the threat from Russia is understood.
She said the Baltic nations — Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania — understand, as do Poland, Romania and Moldova.
Russian President Vladimir Putin "wants to destroy your way of living, your way of functioning, and insert their own chaotic rules into your reality," she said.

Despite the massive increase in defence spending among NATO nations, including Canada, there's no sense of political urgency and frightening lack of resolve in the face of increasing grey zone attacks in Europe.
"Everyone sees the reporting of a lot of the media: this resolve and resilience of the Ukrainian people," she said. "I think that this is also pretty misleading because it serves the purpose of understanding that somehow this conflict, this war, is taken care of and those Ukrainians are carrying on."
North American media, she said, seems to have lost interest in the fate of Ukraine.
"I think everybody is getting used to this war. I don't know what has to happen for us to make it to the front pages. We are dying every single day in the middle of Europe," Klympush-Tsintsadze said.
"We are very, very exhausted."

Going into the summer transfer window as Premier League champions, hope sprang eternal for Arsenal.
An opportunity to capitalise, encouraged by a sense at Emirates Stadium that their competitors were in transition because of managerial instability.
If ever there was a moment to strike in recruitment, this was it.
The plans were ambitious: a shortlist with more than 20 players on it. They were targets at Real Madrid and Atletico Madrid, even at Chelsea and Tottenham.
But as the window shut on Tuesday night, you could not escape the sense of unfulfillment - certainly from a section of supporters.
Arsenal's close season was one characterised by some unquestionable successes, but also riddled by difficulties and frustration.
Ahead of their home match against Chelsea on Sunday, BBC Sport details Arsenal's transfer window and whether manager Mikel Arteta, sporting director Andrea Berta and, perhaps most pertinently, owners Kroenke Sports Entertainment can deem their summer operation a success.
Why it became Guimaraes and not Anderson, Tonali or Scott
Bruno Guimaraes's £75m capture from Newcastle United was Arsenal's most eye-catching signing.
Heading into the summer, Arsenal were keeping abreast of Guimaraes' situation at Newcastle, although others were considered a higher priority.
For instance, their interest in Elliot Anderson was widely reported, but it was clear the England international was joining Manchester City.
Guimaraes' former Newcastle team-mate Sandro Tonali and Bournemouth's Alex Scott were also among the midfielders explored before a move for the South American accelerated.
At the ages of 26 and 23 respectively, Tonali and Scott are younger than Guimaraes, who turns 29 in November.
But numerous factors, including availability and price - Tonali joined Spurs for a minimum £92m - made their signings difficult.
Aston Villa's Amadou Onana was also among the options considered, but the Belgium international suffered a serious knee injury at the World Cup.
By mid-June Guimaraes, who had universal backing inside the Emirates, emerged as the club's primary focus.
Berta knew the player's camp well and Guimaraes was admired by Arteta, who had made it clear he wanted proven talent to take his starting XI - rather than the wider squad - to greater heights.
Berta used his strong relationship with Guimaraes' representatives to facilitate Arsenal's move, hence why Newcastle maintained they had had no direct contact from the London club until days before his move was completed.
It is not uncommon for Berta to lean on intermediaries to conduct negotiations, although the approach has had varying degrees of success.
For instance, Arsenal actively sought moves for Leicester City teenagers Jeremy Monga and Louis Page over the summer.
But sources insist that the lack of club-to-club discussions meant both players ultimately did not join Arsenal, with Monga eventually signing for Manchester City when he appeared to be on the verge of moving to the Emirates.
That said, Berta's success in pivoting the club towards a deal for Guimaraes when it became clear other targets were not viable was well received behind the scenes at Arsenal.
Konsa was first-choice defensive option
The signing of Ezri Konsa was equally complex. Konsa was viewed internally as Arteta's first-choice defensive option.
Arteta wanted players used to the rigours of Premier League football - hence the moves for Guimaraes, Konsa and the failed efforts to land Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa.
Konsa's ability to play at right-back was also viewed as a major benefit. Arsenal considered signing an orthodox right-back, with Ivan Fresneda among the options, but Konsa's versatility was a key factor.
But Berta appeared reluctant to meet Villa's valuation. A week before the Konsa deal was confirmed, Arsenal made a £40m offer, which was duly rejected.
Sources claim the deal was eventually sealed by the ownership at both clubs, and the transfer was agreed at £51m, with £4m in add-ons.
In the event of not reaching an agreement for Konsa, it is understood Tottenham duo Cristian Romero and Micky van der Ven were identified as targets – but Arsenal's north London rivals would not consider selling to them.
Como centre-back Jacobo Ramon is a player the club will continue to monitor, but clauses attached to his current contract make the deal difficult.
Tarik Muharemovic, who joined Leeds United, was another considered.
In attack, Christos Tzolis' impact since arriving from Club Brugge in a deal worth about £35m means the Greece international has been heralded as one of the discoveries of the summer.
It is understood the potential deal for the former Norwich winger was initially raised by an intermediary close to a senior member of the coaching staff during the close season.
Berta's number two, Maurizio Micheli, watched Tzolis play for his country against Sweden in June and was suitably impressed.
So far, the 24-year-old looks a positive addition to Arteta's squad.
Arsenal, who also made Piero Hincapie's loan deal permanent and signed Illan Meslier on a free transfer, are happy with the signings they have made.
The captures of Guimaraes and Konsa, who will both be 30 by the end of next season, have raised eyebrows given the combined £126m fee, amid concerns over how the pair's longevity may impact the natural evolution of the squad.
Yet it is undeniable that Guimares and Konsa add elite quality and experience to Arsenal ranks, and ultimately the club feel they paid the going rate to get those deals over the line.
Arsenal miss out on marque attacker
While the club delivered proven talent for Arteta in defence and midfield, Berta's remit of adding an elite attacker ended in disappointment.
Rogers was the club's primary target heading into the window, and the early indications were positive amid a strongly held view internally that the forward wanted to join.
At the start of the summer, it was Arsenal's understanding that Villa valued Rogers at £100m. Arsenal valued Rogers at £80m.
Berta, however, was confident of negotiating the price down to a level he and the club believed could get the deal done.
In the meantime, however, Berta explored alternatives - Bradley Barcola, Kenan Yildiz, Yan Diomande and Nico Paz were admired.
Anthony Gordon was a long-term target, but he had agreed before the World Cup to join Barcelona.
Yildiz and Paz will continue to be realistic targets moving forward. Eli Junior Kroupi is another the club will watch once he returns from injury for Bournemouth.
Anderson's move from Forest to City for £116m, however, altered the complexion of Villa's outlook on Rogers' future.
Villa increased their valuation to £120m and ultimately Chelsea ended up signing the attacker for £117m.
Arsenal, it is understood, were given the opportunity to match Chelsea's offer but refused, believing their £80m valuation was fair - but it does beg the question of whether Rogers would be a Gunners player now if Berta had acted sooner.
Ultimately, the failure to land Rogers arrived as the first of a series of blows to Berta in his efforts to deliver a top-class left-sided attacker for the team.
Arsenal genuinely believed they had a realistic chance of signing Vinicius Jr before he decided to sign a new contract at Real Madrid.
Berta and Arteta were all in on the Brazil icon. The club were prepared finance the deal too.
While the transfer would likely have cost a British record fee and been one of the most lucrative remuneration packages in Premier League history, the benefit to Arteta's team and the Brazil superstar's commercial value meant Arsenal were absolutely prepared to complete the deal.
Yet well-placed sources expressed to BBC Sport over the summer that Vinicius did not want to leave Real, while others feared Arsenal were being used to strengthen the attacker's efforts to secure a more lucrative contract at the Bernabeu.
Those concerns came to fruition as Vinicius signed a new long-term contract in Spain in another Arsenal disappointment.
There were similar reservations about Arsenal's well-documented pursuit of Julian Alvarez.
The Atletico Madrid forward showed very little indication that he was willing to join Arsenal; his preference to join Barcelona was one of the worst-kept secrets of the window.
But Atletico's point-blank refusal to sell to Barcelona was deemed reason enough by Berta and Arteta to persist with their interest in the hope of Alvarez changing his mind until the closing days of the window.
Alvarez, however, preferred to stay at Atletico, even though his relationship with the club is at an all-time low.
Did Arsenal waste their time with Vinicius and Alvarez? The answer varies depending on who you speak to.
When it became clear Alvarez was unlikely, Berta explored his options.
Intriguingly, Arsenal have admired Chelsea striker Joao Pedro, who was deemed not for sale over the summer, although there were concerns over how he would fit into Arteta's system.
It is claimed Berta relies significantly on his vast network of agent connections rather than acting on the club's existing scouting information when analysing the market.
For example, last summer, when all the scouting information pointed towards a move for Benjamin Sesko, Berta's arrival meant the club pivoted to Viktor Gyokeres, who is currently second-choice striker.
This summer the club's late dalliance with Lyon winger Malick Fofana provided a further example of Berta leaning on his agency connections after management agency Roc Nation offered Arsenal an opportunity to sign the Belgium international.
Berta's relationship with Roc Nation was particularly prevalent this summer given Arsenal's pursuit of Vinicius and the sale of Gabriel Martinelli, who are both clients of the agency.
It remains to be seen how much of an impact Arsenal's failure to sign a recognised top-level attacker impacts their season, particularly in light of Martinelli and Leandro Trossard's departures.
Arsenal will move towards player trading model
Arsenal headed into the window with a clear remit of ensuring the club become more sustainable and adept at trading.
Part of that directive is to ensure the club remain compliant with domestic and European financial regulations.
Depending on who you talk to, the size of the potential deals for Vinicius or Alvarez would have raised doubts over Arsenal's ability to stay within the regulations.
Nevertheless, ensuring they maximised the benefits of player trading will become an increasing part of Arsenal's financial operation in the future.
There was already evidence of that through the sale of Martinelli, whose £60m exit to Al-Hilal was the club's record departure. Arsenal have also secured a sell-on clause in the deal.
The exits of Martinelli, Trossard, Gabriel Jesus, Christian Norgaard, Jakub Kiwior, Fabio Vieira and Karl Hein secured the club in the region of £114m.
Through intermediaries, a possible exit for Myles Lewis-Skelly was explored, with a fee of about £80m believed to have been mooted for the midfielder.
Manchester United, who were attracted to Lewis-Skelly's ability to play at left-back, were interested but ultimately deemed his valuation too high.
Of course, it is Berta's job to have a firm grasp on the level of interest in the club's players and their market value but, nevertheless, the thought of Lewis-Skelly's departure resulted in huge uproar from supporters.
As BBC Sport revealed last month, the Gunners resisted any temptation to sell Ethan Nwaneri on a permanent deal, the academy graduate landing a season-long loan deal to Borussia Dortmund that includes a January recall option if required.
The minimum £15m fee secured in Trossard's deal to Besiktas is also viewed as a good deal inside the Emirates given the Belgian turns 32 in December.
Having spent nearly £450m in 12 months, Berta's work in the market has helped the club deliver their first league title in 22 years.
Yet, despite the money splashed, there remain clear issues in the squad - certainly in attack.
The summer window has left many supporters feeling questioning Berta's body of work at Arsenal.
And with the average age of the squad increasing following the captures of Konsa and Guimaraes, can the current options build a dynasty of success before the club need to spend heavily again on regenerating the team?

భారత స్వాతంత్ర్య ఉద్యమ సమయంలో RSS కార్యకర్తలు బ్రిటన్ రాణికి గౌరవ వందనం చేస్తున్నారంటూ ఒక ఫోటో (ఇక్కడ & ఇక్కడ) సోషల్ మీడియాలో ప్రచారమవుతుంది. ఇందులో ఎంత నిజముందో ఇప్పుడు చూద్దాం.
క్లెయిమ్: RSS కార్యకర్తలు బ్రిటన్ రాణికి గౌరవ వందనం చేస్తున్నప్పటి ఫోటో.
ఫాక్ట్: వైరల్ ఫోటో రెండు వేర్వేరు సందర్భాల్లో తీసిన ఫోటోలను జోడించి ఎడిట్ చేసి సృష్టించబడింది. కావున, పోస్టులో చేయబడిన క్లెయిమ్ తప్పు.
ముందుగా, వైరల్ ఫోటోలో RSS కార్యకర్తలు నిలబడి ఉన్న భాగాన్ని రివర్స్ ఇమేజ్ సెర్చ్ చేయగా, దానికి సంబంధించిన అసలు ఫోటో (ఆర్కైవ్) లభించింది. ఈ ఫోటోను ‘డెక్కన్ క్రానికల్’ వార్తా సంస్థ తమ వెబ్సైట్లో 2016లో ప్రచురించిన ఒక కథనానికి ప్రతీకాత్మక చిత్రంగా ఉపయోగించింది. ఈ ఫోటోలో బ్రిటన్ రాణి లేరు.
ఇక వైరల్ ఫొటోలో బ్రిటన్ రాణి ఉన్న భాగాన్ని రివర్స్ ఇమేజ్ సెర్చ్ చేయగా, దానికి సంబంధించిన అసలు ఫోటో ‘Getty Images’ వెబ్సైట్తో పాటు ‘History Ville‘ అనే ఎక్స్ (X) ఖాతాలో లభించింది. ఆ వివరాల ప్రకారం, 1956లో ఎలిజబెత్-II రాణి నైజీరియా పర్యటనలో నైజీరియా సైనిక దళాలను తనిఖీ చేస్తున్నప్పుడు ఈ ఫోటో తీయబడింది. దీన్ని బట్టి, సంబంధం లేని పై రెండు ఫోటోలను ఎడిట్ చేసి, RSS కార్యకర్తలు బ్రిటన్ రాణికి గౌరవ వందనం చేస్తున్నట్లుగా తప్పుడు ప్రచారం చేస్తున్నారని స్పష్టమవుతుంది.
చివరిగా, RSS కార్యకర్తలు బ్రిటన్ రాణికి గౌరవ వందనం చేస్తున్నట్లుగా చూపుతున్న ఈ ఫోటో ఎడిట్ చేయబడినది.

A nine-second long video clip is has gone viral on social media, showing a man assaulting a puffed rice vendor. In the video, the man is seen overturning the box hanging from the snack seller’s neck and pouring all the food items onto the vendor’s face before they scatter onto the street. As this purported attack unfolds, the vendor stares at the man helplessly.
The video was posted by X user Alka Maurya on September 16 and has garnered more than 2,85,000 views and shared over 1,500 times till publication time. The caption of the post, translated from Hindi, reads: “(He) must be feeling so proud after doing something like this.” (Archive)
कितना गर्व महसूस कर रहा होगा ऐसे करके हैं ना …… pic.twitter.com/F6upi4I2ZD
— Alka Maurya (@MauryaAlka76391) September 16, 2026
Apart from Maurya, film actor Kamaal R Khan posted the same video with the caption: “How will you fix this mentality which has developed in last 10 years. India can’t be fixed now.” (Archive)
How will you fix this mentality which has developed in last 10 years. India can’t be fixed now. pic.twitter.com/o2T2AJzGoj
— KRK (@kamaalrkhan) September 17, 2026
Other social media users circulated the viral clip with similar captions, condemning the man seen purportedly attacking the vendor.
As a billboard visible in the video reads ‘Welcome to Patna Junction’, the Patna police was tagged in the comment section of certain posts, requesting them to take stringent action against the man who allegedly assaulted the vendor.
Fact Check
To verify the authenticity of the viral video clip, we ran reverse image search on several relevant keyframes. It led us to a video posted by content creator Sonu Paswan on Instagram. With 1,79,000 followers, he posts scripted videos highlighting the helpless condition of the working class people in India. Paswan has a social media presence on Facebook and YouTube as well. And according to his social media bios, he is from Darbhanga, Bihar.
In all of his videos, accessible on his Facebook page, Paswan himself can be seen playing different “poor characters” being harassed and attacked by others as he helplessly accepts his fate.
On September 18, Friday, Paswan posted a video on his Instagram page, where he clarified that he enacts emotional scenes on poverty as ‘content’ on his social media platforms. He clarifies that the viral clip does not depict a real attack on him, but is in fact a prepared skit. “I want to tell you that in the video you are seeing, the vendor is me and the man who is attacking me is part of my team. I want to let you know that we, as a team, make emotional videos on poverty. I request you to take this video purely as entertainment, and not believe that this is real,” he said.
The caption of this video reads, translated from Hindi, “Because we make emotional videos on the poor…You all give me so much love…but you guys have taken this clip to heart.
I know I have hurt you guys with this video. Please delete the video from your channel…I request you not to share this video any further.”
View this post on Instagram
After the clip started going viral and attracted significant backlash, on September 17, most of his videos on YouTube and all of his previous videos on Instagram had to be deleted. In the aforementioned video, Paswan urges audiences to not share the viral clip and excerbate his situation even further. “I request you to not share the clip on your personal profiles, please do this much for your brothers,” he said. He shared the same clarification on his YouTube page.
Moreover, Paswan posted videos of the guy who is acting as the attacker in the video, also clarifying the viral clip is indeed a skit, on his Instagram and YouTube pages. “The video you guys are watching and getting emotional and taking to heart is just our content…its not real…please stop roasting this video. Because of you [sharing the viral clip as real] all my efforts have gone to waste, all my videos, over 300 videos…I have had to delete them all. I request you to keep supporting and loving us,” he states in the video.
View this post on Instagram
Given that their skit went viral, misleadingly as a real incident, the content creators said they received backlash and trolling, compelling them to remove their previous videos. At present, Paswan’s Instagram page only features the two clarification videos and his YouTube page features the same. However, his Facebook still displayed his earlier content. The description of his Facebook page, translated from Hindi, also reads: “I make emotional videos on poverty.”
True to the description, Paswan’s Facebook page contains videos similar in theme to the viral video. In these videos, visibly destitute people or poor vendors are seen being humiliated or suffering at the hands of others, while accepting their fate.
Paswan can be identified acting in all of these videos, and a visual match can be established, indicating that he was indeed the person seen in the viral video. Thus, it can be concluded that a scripted video made by a content creator has gone viral, leading netizens to falsely believe that it depicts a real incident of attack on a puffed rice vendor.

All Public Sector Banks and Regional Rural Banks will remain open and function normally on Sunday, September 27, 2026, in view of the proposed three-day nationwide bank strike from September 28 to 30.
The strike has been called by the United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU) and comes after the weekend holidays on September 26 and 27.

The Supreme Court on Wednesday (September 23, 2026) stopped short of requiring Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla to give a specific time line for completing the disqualification proceedings pending against 20 rebel Trinamool Congress party MPs who have aligned themselves with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI).
A three-judge Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant was hearing a plea filed by Trinamool Congress (TMC) leader Abhishek Banerjee contending that Speaker Birla was delaying disqualification proceedings under the anti-defection law.
Mr. Banerjee has sought a time-bound decision on the disqualification of the rebel MPs.
Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Speaker, urged the court to “not fix the Speaker’s schedule”.
This was after Justice Joymalya Bagchi, who is part of the Bench, asked Mr. Mehta to submit a timeline on the disqualification proceedings.
“The Supreme Court monitoring is not necessary,” Mr. Mehta stressed.
Senior advocates Neeraj Kishan Kaul and Maninder Singh, for the rebel MPs, said the Supreme Court monitoring and the three-month time limit highlighted in the Keshab Meghachandra Singh versus Speaker, Manipur Legislative Assembly, was only applicable in cases of “complete inaction” on the part of the Speaker concerned.
“How soon will you file your replies [to the notices issued in the disqualification petitions]?” the Bench asked.
Senior advocate Kalyan Banerjee, appearing for TMC leader Abhishek Banerjee, said the rebel MPs had already got six weeks, and have now sought four weeks more.
The court recorded in the order the MPs’ intention to file their replies in four weeks. It posted the case after four weeks.
Justice Bagchi termed the role of a Speaker as “amphibious”, whose responsibilities concern both the House and as a Tribunal under the Tenth Schedule (anti-defection law) of the Constitution.
The Court had earlier issued notice to the Secretary General and MPs Kakori Ghosh Dastidar, Sudip Bandyopadhyay, Satabdi Roy, Prasun Banerjee, Rachana Banerjee, Jagadish Chandra Barma Basunia, Partha Bhowmick, Arup Chakraborty, Adhikari Deepak Dev, Sayani Ghosh, Bapi Haldar, Md Abu Taher Khan, Kalipada Saren Kherwal, Asit Kumar Mal, June Maliah, Mitali Bag, Khalilur Rahaman, Mala Roy, Sharmila Sarkar and Yusuf Pathan.
The dispute within the party follows a rebellion within the TMC parliamentary party after 20 of its Lok Sabha MPs announced that they had joined or merged with the NCPI, a Tripura-based political outfit, and sought separate recognition in the House.
The rebel MPs had subsequently been treated as an NCPI group in Parliament. They had participated in NDA parliamentary activities.
The TMC has maintained that the MPs were elected on its symbol and that their decision to align with another political formation amounts to voluntarily giving up membership of the party, attracting disqualification under the anti-defection law. The rebel camp has maintained that its move constituted a valid merger.

Steven Sessegnon exclusive: The twin brother of Fulham's Ryan rebuilding at AFC Wimbledon after 'tough' period at Wigan
Steven Sessegnon discusses his 'tough' time at Wigan, returning to his roots to join AFC Wimbledon in the summer, the moment he faced his twin brother Ryan for the first time and more; watch Cambridge vs AFC Wimbledon live on Sky Sports+ on Saturday; kick-off 3pm
Tuesday 22 September 2026 14:20, UK
Steven and Ryan Sessegnon walked out at Craven Cottage side by side, each holding their daughters, last month.
The twins had made their way through Fulham's academy together and played in the first team together on a handful of occasions - but that night, they played against one another for the first time ever.
It was a special moment; a full-circle moment.

In any of the previous three seasons, a game like this would have been a perfect chance for a family reunion, as Steven had been living in Manchester for three years while playing for Wigan.
But now he's back home. And not just 'home' in terms of being back in south-west London. Properly back home.
He points ahead as he speaks to Sky Sports on a terrace at the Dons' training ground in New Malden. "We used to play academy games literally across this grass."
He points to the left. "I spent time at Coombe Boys School, which is five minutes up the road."
Fulham's Motspur Park training ground is six minutes' drive away. There, his nephew Kayden is part of the U18 squad.
"It's really wholesome to be back," says Sessegnon. "It helps massively being around family.
"I get to see my older brothers, my nieces, my nephews and I see my brother [Ryan] a few times a week.
"We play at two different levels, so there isn't too much to speak about as if we were in the same league, but we catch up on life, being dads, being providers, being men in our families and what the future looks like."
Sessegnon's return home has come at an important point in his career.
In his first season at Wigan in 2023/24, he played 29 games in all competitions. In his second, he suffered calf and knee injuries, before not playing again from January 4 2025.
At the start of his third, Gary Caldwell, who had replaced Ryan Lowe in February 2025, placed him on the transfer list.
"Things happen fast in football," Sessegnon says. "When I was put on the transfer list, I was told I wasn't going to play and I didn't go on the pre-season trip - but I ended up starting the first game of the season through injuries or lack of availability, and I thought I did well.
"It's fair game, it's part of it. The manager came in, the club wanted to go in a different direction. As long as everyone can come out of it happy and people can move onto clubs they know they can do well at, there's no problem with it."
A move away did not materialise so, on the few occasions Caldwell did select him, he was deployed at centre-back, where he had never played before.
"It was tough. Very, very tough. I felt like I could contribute to a team, but didn't really have the trust or belief behind me to do it.
"But as much as I could say I didn't have the proper backing to be in my own position, I was still given a chance to play football. It was down to me and it just never happened.
"There was no issue with anyone else apart from myself. I learned a lot there, a lot I can take with me for the rest of my career. It was a learning curve.
"The biggest thing was professionalism. Even in the worst stages of when I wasn't playing and I was told I wasn't going to be a part of it, I could still carry myself and be the best possible person.
"I felt I owed it to myself to show people I was still a very good trainer, a very good player and I think that helped me stick around longer than they probably wanted me to."
Sessegnon was released by the Latics in the summer and joined AFC Wimbledon on a two-year contract, with the option for a further 12 months, on June 25.
"I was preparing to go on holiday with my family and I got a call. As soon as they said Wimbledon, local, I said 'let's get it sorted'," he recalls.
"But it was also about the position I would play, how the gaffer [Johnnie Jackson] set it out. It wasn't complicated. I knew I could come in and, if I could get minutes, I would show my ability."
Sessegnon's first Dons appearance came on August 8 against Newport in the Carabao Cup, almost six months after his last competitive game for Wigan. He looks in genuine disbelief when he hears that.
His full league debut came on September 7, in a 2-0 Sky Bet League One win over Bromley. He has had to bide his time, but he understands why.
"It's like injuries, you have a bit of anxiousness about getting going again, but I had the pre-season and here at Wimbledon, they looked after me very well. The gaffer has looked after me very well and communicated very well with me.
"In my head I wanted to start and play as many games as I could, but coming off the bench a few times has probably benefitted me to get to grips with football again.
"It's probably the simplest football I've played in my career, but the most effective. We're able to create chances, I'm able to get the ball high up the pitch.
"It's not overthought, and I think it brings the best out of the whole squad and definitely myself. I've enjoyed it so far and it takes the pressure off the whole squad; we know we can create chances, we just have to be solid."
The Dons have certainly been solid, with five clean sheets from seven games so far - the joint-most in the Sky Bet EFL.
They are four points behind leaders Bradford going into Saturday's trip to Cambridge - which is live on Sky Sports+ - despite having only scored five goals so far.
That said, they are still among the bookmakers' favourites to be relegated this season.
But now, back on home soil, Sessegnon has the chance to help AFC Wimbledon defy the odds again, just around the corner from where it all began.

Ronaldo has scored 979 goals for club and country in his career; the 41-year-old forward, who plays for Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia, says it would be "beautiful" to score his 1,000th goal in a Portugal shirt

Cristiano Ronaldo considered retiring from international football after the World Cup before deciding to extend his Portugal career.
Ronaldo - who turns 42 in February - will win his 234th cap against Wales in Lisbon on Thursday, with Portugal head coach Jorge Jesus confirming that the former Manchester United and Real Madrid will start the Nations League fixture.
Some commentators have suggested the game at the Jose Alvalade Stadium - the home of Ronaldo's first club Sporting - could be his international farewell, but the five-time Ballon d'Or winner said he will finish when "I feel like I'm not doing anything here".

Age seemed to have caught up with Ronaldo this summer during a World Cup when many of the game's greatest stars shone on its biggest stage, leading to speculation that his international career had run its course.
Asked if he considered leaving Portugal after the World Cup, Ronaldo said: "Yes I did. Of course, I'm always thinking on my decisions, my future, the present also.
"I'm a thinker. You have to think. This is why you see me here now. It means I will continue.
"I had a conversation with our president, with our coach. I still believe that I'm able to help the national team to reach what they want, and will finish when I feel like I'm not doing anything here.
"I can give to the national team my support, not only through the goals, but also outside of football.

Ronaldo, playing for Al Nassr in Saudi Arabia, currently has 979 career goals.
He denied that he is obsessed with reaching 1,000 goals, although he did add he would love to reach the landmark in Portugal colours.
"Scoring my 1,000th goal for the national team would be the culmination of something - a beautiful story," he said. "It wouldn't be the end of it, but it would be a beautiful story.
"I've already admitted that I want to get there, and I will get there. An obsession? No. The rest is about enjoying it, enjoying every day.
"I know why young kids love Cristiano, because they see me as an example, and I will continue to do that. Even when I am retired... in 10 years.
"I'm happy with myself. It doesn't matter if I play tomorrow, if I rest the next game, for me the most important thing is that I feel good."

England players carrying World Cup scar - Saka

England winger Bukayo Saka says the team are still carrying the "scar" of their heartbreaking World Cup semi-final exit to Argentina.
Thomas Tuchel's team were on the verge of becoming the first England side to reach a men's World Cup final since 1966, but were stunned by two late Argentina goals as they fell to a 2-1 loss.

"We are trying to draw a line under [the World Cup] now and focus on the new international season that we have coming up," Saka added.
"We have got four massive, difficult group games to try and qualify us for the Nations League [knockouts] that we are really focused on."
